newsitem.title: MEXICO: Six gunned down at restaurant in northern Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Six gunned down at restaurant in northern Mexico.

text.p: Gunmen walked calmly into a smart restaurant in this northern Mexico border city and shot dead six people in an attack police believe was part of a drug-trafficking turf war.
Police spokesman Ernesto Garcia said on Monday that two gunmen pulled up outside the Maxfim restaurant in a black sports car on Sunday evening and went inside, walking straight to the bathroom.
Moments later, they came out blasting with powerful assault rifles, killing four men and two women, and wounding three others before escaping.
"All of the victims had several bullet wounds in the chest and head area," Garcia said. "Because of the way it was done, it appears to be related to narco-trafficking."
Arturo Tobar, a homicide detective with the State Judicial Police, said one of the dead men was Fernando Olague, a senior jail guard at the Cereso prison in Ciudad Juarez.

He said Olague was shot inside the restaurant but then pulled a pistol and tried to escape onto the street. He made it as far as the street corner before falling dead on the pavement, his gun by his side.
Garcia had earlier said Olague appeared to have been an innocent bystander.
He said one of the dead women was apparently not part of the group that was targeted in the attack. "She happened to be in the wrong place at the wrong time."
Ciudad Juarez, which lies just across the border from El Paso, Texas, is a major drug trafficking centre for gangs smuggling cocaine into the United States.
The so-called Juarez drug cartel was run by Amado Carrillo Fuentes, Mexico's most wanted drug criminal until his sudden death last month after undergoing plastic surgery.
Since Carrillo's death the murder rate in Ciudad Juarez and other drug hot spots along the U.S.-Mexico border has soared in what experts describe as feuding between mid-level cartel hoodlums.
Even before Sunday's attack, U.S. anti-narcotics officials said up to a dozen people may have been killed in Ciudad Juarez alone in the turf battles since Carillo's death.
The Maxfim restaurant, which lies across the street from the bullring in downtown Ciudad Juarez, was remodeled and opened about three months ago.
